value.name: Oregon Solar + Storage Rebate Program (OSSRP) — Energy Storage System
value.description: Statewide Oregon rebate for residential energy storage systems paired with a solar electric system: $300 per kWh of installed storage capacity, up to 60% of net system cost or $2,500 (whichever is less) for low/moderate-income homeowners, or up to 40% of net cost or $2,500 for other homeowners. Rebates are issued to ODOE-approved contractors, who pass savings to the customer at time of installation (no upfront payment/reimbursement wait). System must have 'islanding' capability. As of this record's verification date (June 2026 update on ODOE's own page), the program is NOT currently accepting new rebate reservation applications — the $1.1 million reopened on June 15, 2026 was fully reserved almost immediately. This is a genuine, temporary funding-exhaustion pause, not a program termination.
value.eligibility: Must be installed on Oregon real property by an ODOE-approved contractor; storage must be paired at time of installation with a previously purchased/installed (or concurrently purchased) solar electric system; reservation application required before construction begins.

battery_programs.notes: Verified directly from the Oregon Dept. of Energy's own page, including its own explicit June 2026 update that the program is temporarily not accepting new reservations due to full subscription — recorded as 'active' (the program itself remains legally established and is expected to reopen) rather than 'expired', with the funding-pause caveat preserved in the description rather than omitted.

value.program_or_pathway: Prescriptive vs. Engineered Systems solar permit pathways
other_conditions: Two distinct review pathways: Prescriptive (roof meets prescriptive standards per the state building code; does not require an Oregon-registered design professional) and Engineered Systems (does require a registered design professional)

Solar roof tile installations must follow the Engineered Systems process, but are exempt from the registered-design-professional and engineering-calculation requirements if: net installed weight of all above-sheathing components ≤4 psf; tiles are installed directly over existing sheathing with all prior roofing material removed; and all tiles (active and inactive) are uniformly supported over the sheathing — per ORSC Section 905.16 (2021) / OSSC Section 1507.16 (2022)
A free 15-minute pre-application question appointment is available with a City planner, permit technician, building code/engineering reviewer, or fire safety expert

value.name: Oregon Solar + Storage Rebate Program (OSSRP) — Solar Electric System
value.description: Statewide Oregon rebate for residential solar electric systems: low/moderate-income homeowners receive $1.80/watt(DC), up to 60% of net cost or $5,000 (whichever is less); homeowners not low/moderate-income but eligible for a utility incentive receive $0.20/watt(DC) up to 40% of net cost or $5,000; homeowners not eligible for a utility incentive receive $0.50/watt(DC) up to 40% of net cost or $5,000. 'Net cost' excludes any utility or Energy Trust of Oregon incentive already applied. Rebates are issued to ODOE-approved contractors, who pass savings to the customer directly (no reimbursement wait). As of this record's verification date (June 2026 update on ODOE's own page), the program is NOT currently accepting new rebate reservation applications — the $1.1 million reopened on June 15, 2026 was fully reserved almost immediately. This is a genuine, temporary funding-exhaustion pause, not a program termination.
value.eligibility: Must be installed on Oregon real property by an ODOE-approved contractor; reservation application required before construction begins; must meet minimum Total Solar Resource Fraction and other technical criteria.

rebates.notes: Verified directly from the Oregon Dept. of Energy's own page. The $1.80/watt figure recorded here is specifically the low/moderate-income tier (the highest of the three tiers); the two non-LMI tiers ($0.20/W and $0.50/W, both also capped at $5,000/40% of net cost) are described in full in the description field rather than as separate program entries, since they are variations of the same single program rather than genuinely distinct programs.
